answer: Inter-arrival histogram gating. Each identity must build a request-timing profile matching organic traffic: human-velocity bursts with velvet-smooth idle gaps. A new identity whose first 200 actions arrive on a fixed cadence—say, one per 400ms—gets throttled to a slow onboarding lane until its histogram diverges from machine regularity. The signal is variance in inter-action delay, not volume. Enforcing this costs a sybil farm one plausible human pacing per identity, including randomized pauses and karst-like irregularity, roughly 10x the compute of a naive bot loop.
